sources.locator: RBLA 2011 reprint p. 241; also listed among the ~40 Tupí-Guaraní languages p. 237; source note in references p. 249; Nimuendajú 1932 (Takunyapé)
sources.note: This work describes Takunyapé (listed only; no forms or prosodic data given). Takunyapé occurs three times: in the inventory of Tupí-Guaraní languages (p. 237), as a member of Subconjunto VIII (p. 241), and as the language tagged on the Nimuendajú 1932 reference (p. 249). No Takunyapé word forms are cited anywhere and nothing is said about its stress, accent or tone; the diagnostic features of Subconjunto VIII are segmental only (final consonants, *tx/*ts, *pw, *pj, *j). The work is a subgrouping proposal, not a description; the only Takunyapé data behind it are Nimuendajú 1932 (cited). Compa…

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center (Reference Series 7). Entry 'Tacuñapé or Eidum or Péua', p. 112; comparative table p. 113, column TAKUNAPE.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads 'extinct language once spoken on the Iririru and Novo Rivers. [Nimuendajú 1932b, p. 547, only a few words.]'; the table gives c. 10 comparative items (tatá, ika, kuná, tapií..). Classification only.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1932. Idiomas indígenas del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2(2): 543-618. Section 'Die Takunyape', pp. 543-547 (German), wordlist p. 547.
sources.note: Nothing. Four pages of ethnohistory plus c. 40 words recalled from memory by three settlers (Accioly, de Castro, Pinheiro) decades after the tribe died out; Nimuendajú warns 'deren Aussprache jedoch wohl recht mangelhaft gewesen sein dürfte' and that he knows no other records. Forms are printed with acute accents (kuarí, tupá, amán, yapepó, iká, marapé, tapií, akikí, arapayá, irirí, tairí, katú), mostly on the final vowel, but there is no diacritics key for this section and no remark on accent. sources.citation: Coudreau, Henri. 1897. Voyage au Xingú (30 mai 1896 - 26 octobre 1896). Paris: Lahure.
sources.note: Coudreau met the last c. 40 Takunyapé in 1894-96 (Nimuendajú 1932: 546 cites him pp. 20, 33); his Xingu volumes carry vocabularies of other tribes and could conceivably hold a few Takunyapé words with accent marks. Nimuendajú, who read it, says he knew of no other record, and Loukotka cites only Nimuendajú, so the chance is low.
